investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the two nodes advertising the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence was collected (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState all missing), confirming the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource but reported it as exhausted (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the other four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the two eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for 131–145 seconds across all three sibling checks before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence output and failing every contract assertion. This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource were fully exhausted, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence was collected by any check, and the contract's five required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are entirely absent because the agent pod never started.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm (the peer-pod VM resource is at capacity), and four nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. Because the pod never became Running, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1918) never completed, no agent was provisioned, and the eval produced zero evidence — failing the expected-output contract for orgId, agentId, model, provider, and message. This is an eval-infrastructure / cluster-capacity failure, not a confirmed user-facing product outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

Secondary: Node affinity or node selector misconfiguration on the submitted pod — the four remaining nodes are excluded by label selectors or affinity rules, concentrating all remote-agent scheduling onto only the two kata-capable nodes and making the cluster more sensitive to capacity pressure.

Tertiary: A recent increase in concurrent remote agent workloads (e.g., from other eval runs, user sessions, or background jobs) consumed the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota before this eval's pods were submitted.

Lower confidence: A cluster-level change (node drain, node removal, or resource quota adjustment) reduced the effective kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity without a corresponding scale-out — no cluster change evidence is present in the supplied packet, so this remains speculative.
